If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overreaction.  
If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.3) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.  
When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 5 days, shift forecast downward by 2–3% in the 16–30 day horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.67) and price is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per week to avoid momentum overfitting.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per week to avoid underestimating bearish momentum.  
For late horizon (21–30 days), if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is above true path, apply a 1–2% downward correction to align with sentiment drift.
